text:
Jules: handing off to @Maya for the midday shift — quick consolidated recap below. TL;DR: embeddings latency spike during EU morning window, partial customer impact for two high-throughput tenants, mitigation performed (fallback routing + temporary token-bucket relax), metrics stable now, follow-ups listed.

Jules: timeline (brief):
- 04:03 UTC: alert: p95 embeddings latency rose from ~120ms -> ~1.2s (alerts triggered).
- 04:05 UTC: automated fallback routed ~10% of traffic to smaller quantized model (model-q4f) per emergency policy.
- 04:09 UTC: cache leader churn observed in eu-west cluster (increased KV eviction rate).
- 04:12 UTC: ops page to oncall; I bridged and called for priority throttle and temporary token-bucket increase for two affected customers.
- 04:20 UTC: rate-normalized & latency trending down; by 04:40 UTC p95 back to ~180ms.

Jules: customer impact summary:
- Affected: Customer A (analytics pipeline) and Customer B (internal partner) saw request retries and slow embeddings for ~15-35 minutes. Both reported increased client-side retries. No material data loss. Escalated to CS and account owners.
- Mitigation prevented broader impact across other tenants.

Jules: what we changed during the incident (actions taken):
- Enabled emergency routing via `routing-policy emergency-eu-fallback` to shift 10% -> model-q4f.
- Increased token-bucket for tenant-A and tenant-B to allow short burst while we stabilized: `redwoodctl quota tenant-A --burst +2000` and similar for tenant-B.
- Forced a cache leader election on eu-west KV cluster: `kvctl elect-leader eu-west-1 --force` (this reduced eviction tail).
- Rolled a hotfix to batcher config to reduce big-request batching window from 120ms -> 60ms for eu-west for 30min (to reduce amplification).

Jules: runbook pointers used:
- Embeddings latency playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-latency (followed section 2.1 emergency fallback).
- KV cache leader troubleshooting: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-leader-elections
- Routing policies quick ref: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-policies

Jules: outstanding items and next steps (handoff to Maya / Lin):
- Root cause investigation: engineering (eng-runtime + eng-ml) to correlate request-size histogram to eviction events. I created an investigation ticket: INC-2026-1187.
- Postmortem owner: Lin volunteered to coordinate — please confirm, Lin? (needs to include customer impact timeline and decisions).
- Short-term config: decide whether to make the batcher window change permanent for eu-west — need perf team input.
- Follow-up with CS to confirm customers are OK and reduce any follow-on escalations (Jules already pinged CS).
- Add a canary for KV leader stability: create a synthetic that hits a small cache key set and alerts on eviction rate > 3% for 5m.

Maya: ack — taking primary now. I have local access to eu-west infra and will monitor the dashboards for 2h. I also synced with SRE to ensure the hotfix reverts automatically in 3h if not locked in.

Maya: immediate playbook items I will run first:
- Verify `kv_eviction_rate` is stable under 1% across eu-west leader nodes.
- Confirm model-q4f latency remains within expected bounds for production traffic.
- Keep routing-policy `emergency-eu-fallback` at 10% unless we see client errors for q4f.

Raj: I'll be secondary for the next 4 hours. I'll take charge of the postmortem doc and start drafting timeline + customer comms template. Raj: noted.

Lin: I'll own the postmortem write-up and coordinate with CS + eng-ml for root cause analysis. I'll link the doc in this thread when I have a first draft.

oncall-bot: Reminder — incident INC-2026-1187 created by Jules at 1990012460. Pager duty entries updated.

Maya: a few operational notes / commands I used during mitigation (for the record):
```
# routing change
redwoodctl routing apply --policy emergency-eu-fallback --percent 10
# increase burst for tenant
redwoodctl quota set tenant-A --burst 2000
# check kv eviction rate
promql: rate(kv_evictions_total{region="eu-west"}[5m]) / kube_pod_info
```

Maya: monitoring links (read-only):
- Embeddings p95 + histograms: https://grafana.internal/d/embeddings/eu-west?orgId=1
- KV dashboard (evictions, leader): https://grafana.internal/d/kv/evictions
- Routing policy status: https://console.redwood/routing/emergency-eu-fallback

Jules: notes for postmortem that might help (copied from my incident log):
- We observed a short window where aggregate request-size 99th percentile doubled due to a customer batch job. That appears to have amplified KV eviction pressure.
- The automatic fallback policy performed as intended and bounded blast radius; without it many more tenants would've seen degraded p95.
- The batcher amplification heuristic needs review — large single requests should be capped or routed differently to avoid mass eviction cascades.

Maya: handoff checklist completed:
- Primary: Maya (ACK)
- Secondary: Raj (ACK)
- Postmortem owner: Lin (ACK)
- Customer contacts: CS assigned
- Runbooks referenced: embeddings-latency, kv-leader-elections

Maya: I will stay on this thread and post status updates every 30 minutes for the next 2 hours, or earlier if anything changes.

Raj: quick question — do we want to add a metric alert for percent of traffic routed to fallback model > 5% sustained for 5m? That would catch larger incidents earlier.

Jules: +1 to Raj. I filed a follow-up ticket: OPS-2026-432 to add that alert and tag eng-runtime.

Lin: acknowledged. I'll include all config diffs, command history, and a timeline in the postmortem. Planning to post a first draft inside 24h.

Maya: thanks team — handing on. :thumbsup:

Jules: thanks for taking over, Maya. Leaving my console open for any quick context follow-ups.

(End of thread)
